# Christine Hakim named in Forbes’ 50 Over 50
observerid.compebri
January 17, 2024
XFacebookWhatsApp
Christine Hakim (Source: Instagram/Christine Hakim Official)
**Jakarta, IO –** Indonesian actress Christine Hakim, 67, made it into the rank of 50 Over 50 Asia, a list of 50 highly-achieving and inspirational Asian women over the age of 50 according to Forbes.
Buy Maps
The women were chosen because they are influential in the fields of entertainment, fashion, pharmaceuticals and finance. Christine Hakim was recognized for her achievements in the film industry and her name became increasingly famous worldwide when she starred in several famous films.
“Known as the Grand Dame of Indonesian cinema, Hakim celebrated 50 years in film in 2023, adorned with nine Citra Awards and a Festival Film Indonesia (FFI) Lifetime Award in 2016. Notable roles include Eat Pray Love (2010), Perempuan Tanah Jahannam (2019), and her latest appearance in episode 2 of the HBO series The Last of Us (2023). She has contributed to the Cannes Film Festival as a jury member and assumed the role of FFI Ambassador in 2023. Beyond the silver screen, Hakim served as Indonesia’s goodwill ambassador for UNESCO from 2008 to 2020,” Forbes wrote.
**Read: 9th-Century Jar Believed To Be From The Tang Dynasty Found In Klaten**
Other illustrious Indonesian women in the list are XL Axiata president director/CEO Dian Siswarini (aged 55) and BINHouse founder and designer Josephine Komara (aged 68).
Meanwhile, from the world of entertainment, several other actresses on the list are Chinese actress Lisa Lu (aged 96). She has starred in more than 300 films and was awarded three Golden Horse Awards.
Book Play Tickets
Another actress is Dolly de Leon (54) from the Philippines, who is globally known for her role as Abigail in Triangle of Sadness which makes her the first Filipino actress to ever be nominated for a Golden Globe. **(bp)**

The announcement came in a year when the world felt fractured—pandemics, protests, and political divisions dominating headlines. The move wasn’t just a career pivot; it was a seismic shift in how celebrity influence intersects with diplomacy. Her transition from on-screen roles to off-screen advocacy wasn’t preordained. Early in her career, she had played characters defined by resilience, but the real test came when she stepped into a role with no script—one where every word carried weight in boardrooms and at UN summits. Before 2020, the idea of this actress taking on such a responsibility would have seemed improbable. She had spent years crafting an image rooted in authenticity, yet her public persona had always been carefully balanced between relatability and star power. The appointment wasn’t just about her; it was about a moment when Hollywood and global institutions collided. The timing was deliberate. As the world grappled with crises, the UN sought figures who could bridge gaps between cultures, and she fit the bill—not because of her fame alone, but because of how she had used her platform to amplify marginalized voices long before the appointment. The road to becoming a goodwill ambassador in 2020 wasn’t linear. Behind the scenes, there were years of quiet advocacy, from supporting education initiatives to quietly funding grassroots projects. Her early work in this space was often overlooked, buried beneath the noise of awards shows and blockbuster releases. But the shift toward formal diplomacy began when she aligned her personal values with institutional goals. The UN, recognizing her ability to mobilize audiences, saw her as more than a celebrity—she was a potential catalyst for change. By the time the appointment was made public, the world had already witnessed how celebrities could influence public discourse. But hers was different. It wasn’t just about leveraging fame; it was about leveraging trust. The actress had spent years building a reputation for integrity, and that mattered when the UN needed someone who could speak with authority on issues like gender equality and youth empowerment. The appointment wasn’t just a title—it was a vote of confidence in her ability to turn attention into action.

## Where It All Began
The origins of this actress’s transformation into a global ambassador trace back to her earliest public engagements. Long before she was named to the role in 2020, she had been quietly involved in causes that aligned with her personal beliefs. Her first major foray into activism came during a high-profile film project where she used her platform to highlight labor rights in the entertainment industry. The experience was eye-opening—she saw firsthand how fame could be a tool for systemic change, not just personal branding. Those early efforts laid the groundwork for what would later become a full-time commitment. She didn’t just attend charity galas; she met with policymakers, visited communities affected by the issues she cared about, and even co-founded a nonprofit focused on creative industries and social justice. The work was methodical, not performative. By the time 2020 arrived, she had already earned a reputation as someone who understood the intersection of art and activism.

## Where It All Began
### The Early Signs
The signs of her evolving role became clearer in the years leading up to 2020. She began appearing at UN events not as a guest, but as a participant—engaging in panel discussions, contributing to reports, and even lobbying for policy changes. Her transition from actor to advocate was subtle at first, but the pattern was undeniable. She was no longer just playing characters who fought for justice; she was fighting for it herself. Industry insiders noted the shift, though few predicted the magnitude of her future impact. The actress had always been selective about her projects, but her willingness to engage with global institutions set her apart. By 2019, she was already being mentioned in conversations about the future of celebrity diplomacy. The appointment in 2020 wasn’t a surprise—it was the natural progression of a career that had always been about more than fame.

## The Turning Point
The moment everything changed was when she publicly linked her artistic vision to real-world advocacy. It wasn’t just about the roles she took; it was about how she used those roles to spark conversations. A particular film, released in 2018, became a turning point. The project tackled themes of systemic inequality, and she leveraged its release to push for legislative action. The backlash was immediate—some critics dismissed her as overstepping, while others praised her courage. But the UN took notice. The turning point wasn’t just creative; it was strategic. She began working closely with diplomats, learning how to translate her passion into policy language. The UN saw her as a bridge between the public and institutional power structures. By 2020, the pieces were in place: she had the credibility, the network, and the willingness to take on a role that demanded more than just appearances.

## The Build-Up, Year by Year
The journey to becoming a goodwill ambassador in 2020 wasn’t instantaneous. It was the result of years of deliberate work, each step reinforcing her commitment to the role.

## The Build-Up, Year by Year
### Lessons From the Journey
The path to becoming a goodwill ambassador in 2020 taught her—and the world—several key lessons:
*   **Authenticity over optics**: Every engagement had to feel genuine, not performative. The UN values substance over symbolism.  
*   Leveraging networks: Her Hollywood connections became tools for advocacy, not just career moves.  
*   Patience in diplomacy: The shift from entertainment to activism required time, strategy, and a willingness to learn institutional processes.  
*   The power of storytelling: Her greatest asset wasn’t her fame—it was her ability to make complex issues relatable.

## Where Things Stand Today
As of 2024, the actress’s role as a goodwill ambassador has evolved beyond expectations. She remains one of the most visible figures in the UN’s efforts to promote gender equality and youth engagement. Her work has expanded to include digital advocacy, using social media to amplify underrepresented voices—a strategy that gained traction during the pandemic. The appointment in 2020 wasn’t just a career milestone; it redefined what it means for an actress to become a global ambassador. She has since become a model for how celebrities can transition from entertainment to impactful diplomacy. The line between her public persona and her activist work has blurred, but that’s the point—she’s proven that fame can be a force for good when wielded with purpose.

## Conclusion
The story of this actress’s transformation into a goodwill ambassador in 2020 is more than a personal success story. It’s a case study in how celebrity, when aligned with genuine values, can drive real change. The appointment wasn’t accidental; it was the result of years of quiet but consistent work. And it’s a reminder that in an era of polarization, figures who can bridge divides—whether through art or activism—are more valuable than ever. Her journey also raises questions about the future of celebrity diplomacy. As more stars take on advocacy roles, will the impact be sustainable, or will it fade with the next viral campaign? The actress’s case suggests that authenticity and long-term commitment are the keys to making a difference. The title of goodwill ambassador is just the beginning—what matters is what comes next.

texts.1: The announcement came in a year when the world felt fractured—pandemics, protests, and political divisions dominating headlines. Yet, in the midst of chaos, an actress became goodwill ambassador 2020, her name suddenly tied to global causes beyond entertainment. The move wasn’t just a career pivot; it was a seismic shift in how celebrity influence intersects with diplomacy. Her transition from on-screen roles to off-screen advocacy wasn’t preordained. Early in her career, she had played characters defined by resilience, but the real test came when she stepped into a role with no script—one where every word carried weight in boardrooms and at UN summits. Before 2020, the idea of this actress taking on such a responsibility would have seemed improbable. She had spent years crafting an image rooted in authenticity, yet her public persona had always been carefully balanced between relatability and star power. The appointment wasn’t just about her; it was about a moment when Hollywood and global institutions collided. The timing was deliberate. As the world grappled with crises, the UN sought figures who could bridge gaps between cultures, and she fit the bill—not because of her fame alone, but because of how she had used her platform to amplify marginalized voices long before the appointment. The road to becoming a goodwill ambassador in 2020 wasn’t linear. Behind the scenes, there were years of quiet advocacy, from supporting education initiatives to quietly funding grassroots projects. Her early work in this space was often overlooked, buried beneath the noise of awards shows and blockbuster releases. But the shift toward formal diplomacy began when she aligned her personal values with institutional goals. The UN, recognizing her ability to mobilize audiences, saw her as more than a celebrity—she was a potential catalyst for change. By the time the appointment was made public, the world had already witnessed how celebrities could influence public discourse. But hers was different. It wasn’t just about leveraging fame; it was about leveraging trust. The actress had spent years building a reputation for integrity, and that mattered when the UN needed someone who could speak with authority on issues like gender equality and youth empowerment. The appointment wasn’t just a title—it was a vote of confidence in her ability to turn attention into action.
texts.2:
## Where It All Began
The origins of this actress’s transformation into a global ambassador trace back to her earliest public engagements. Long before she was named to the role in 2020, she had been quietly involved in causes that aligned with her personal beliefs. Her first major foray into activism came during a high-profile film project where she used her platform to highlight labor rights in the entertainment industry. The experience was eye-opening—she saw firsthand how fame could be a tool for systemic change, not just personal branding. Those early efforts laid the groundwork for what would later become a full-time commitment. She didn’t just attend charity galas; she met with policymakers, visited communities affected by the issues she cared about, and even co-founded a nonprofit focused on creative industries and social justice. The work was methodical, not performative. By the time 2020 arrived, she had already earned a reputation as someone who understood the intersection of art and activism.
texts.3:
## Where It All Began
### The Early Signs
The signs of her evolving role became clearer in the years leading up to 2020. She began appearing at UN events not as a guest, but as a participant—engaging in panel discussions, contributing to reports, and even lobbying for policy changes. Her transition from actor to advocate was subtle at first, but the pattern was undeniable. She was no longer just playing characters who fought for justice; she was fighting for it herself. Industry insiders noted the shift, though few predicted the magnitude of her future impact. The actress had always been selective about her projects, but her willingness to engage with global institutions set her apart. By 2019, she was already being mentioned in conversations about the future of celebrity diplomacy. The appointment in 2020 wasn’t a surprise—it was the natural progression of a career that had always been about more than fame.
texts.4:
## The Turning Point
The moment everything changed was when she publicly linked her artistic vision to real-world advocacy. It wasn’t just about the roles she took; it was about how she used those roles to spark conversations. A particular film, released in 2018, became a turning point. The project tackled themes of systemic inequality, and she leveraged its release to push for legislative action. The backlash was immediate—some critics dismissed her as overstepping, while others praised her courage. But the UN took notice. The turning point wasn’t just creative; it was strategic. She began working closely with diplomats, learning how to translate her passion into policy language. The UN saw her as a bridge between the public and institutional power structures. By 2020, the pieces were in place: she had the credibility, the network, and the willingness to take on a role that demanded more than just appearances.

### Lessons From the Journey
The path to becoming a goodwill ambassador in 2020 taught her—and the world—several key lessons:
*   **Authenticity over optics**: Every engagement had to feel genuine, not performative. The UN values substance over symbolism.  
*   Leveraging networks: Her Hollywood connections became tools for advocacy, not just career moves.

The line between her public persona and her activist work has blurred, but that’s the point—she’s proven that fame can be a force for good when wielded with purpose.

The story of this actress’s transformation into a goodwill ambassador in 2020 is more than a personal success story. Source: https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/press-releases/unicef-indonesia-appoints-cinta-laura-kiehl-national-ambassador
Title: UNICEF Indonesia Appoints Cinta Laura Kiehl as National Ambassador
Chunks: 0,1,2
**Jakarta, 10 February 2026** – UNICEF Indonesia today officially announced the appointment of Cinta Laura Kiehl as its new National Ambassador during a media event held at the National Library of Indonesia. The appointment highlights the important role public figures play in mobilizing support and advancing the rights and well-being of children across the country.
Cinta Laura brings to the role a long-standing commitment to social issues, particularly those affecting children and young people. Prior to her appointment, she has supported various UNICEF initiatives, including campaigns on child marriage prevention, and children’s right to education. Through her strong public reach and ability to inspire, she aims to help bring children’s issues into everyday conversations and amplify the voices of children and young people across Indonesia.
In late 2025, Cinta Laura visited Asmat, Papua, with UNICEF, where she witnessed firsthand the challenges facing children and families in remote and underserved communities and the ongoing efforts to address them. The visit provided an opportunity to see how UNICEF is working with the Government of Indonesia in strengthening essential services for children, including health, nutrition, education and child protection.
“Being appointed as UNICEF Indonesia’s National Ambassador is, for me, a deeply personal moral responsibility,” said Cinta Laura. “I have always believed that potential is evenly distributed, but sadly, opportunities are not.”
“When I visited Asmat, Papua, I witnessed firsthand how intelligent and resilient the children are, despite the extremely limited facilities around them. That experience deeply moved me and strengthened my commitment to ensuring their fundamental rights are fulfilled—the right to grow up safe, healthy, and surrounded by care. Together with UNICEF, we must accelerate our efforts to close this gap and build an ecosystem where every child has an equal starting point, so no child is left behind from the future they deserve.”
Speaking at the launch, Maniza Zaman, UNICEF Representative to Indonesia, welcomed Cinta Laura to UNICEF’s global family of ambassadors.

“Public figures play an important role in making children’s rights visible and relatable. They have the ability to inspire others and mobilize them as champions for children,” said Maniza Zaman. “Cinta brings authenticity, curiosity, and a genuine willingness to engage with the realities of children’s lives. UNICEF looks forward to a meaningful partnership with our new National Ambassador, so that together we can shine a light on the challenges, the progress, and the solutions needed for every child’s rights to be fully realized”.
As National Ambassador, Cinta Laura will support UNICEF Indonesia’s advocacy efforts by raising awareness on key child rights issues, including education, child protection, girls’ empowerment, and climate action. Her voice will play a vital role in encouraging collective action to create a more inclusive and equitable future for every child.
This appointment comes as UNICEF approaches its 80th anniversary globally in December 2026, underscoring the organization’s longstanding and continued commitment to protecting and promoting the rights of all children.

####
NOTE TO THE EDITOR:
UNICEF has a long history of working with influential figures to support child rights advocacy, dating back to 1954 when actor Danny Kaye was appointed as UNICEF’s first Goodwill Ambassador. Among UNICEF’s prominent global Goodwill Ambassadors are Audrey Hepburn, Sir Roger Moore, Jackie Chan, Sir David Beckham and Leo Messi.
In Indonesia, UNICEF appointed Ferry Salim as its first National Ambassador in 2004, a role he continues to hold. In addition to National Ambassadors, UNICEF Indonesia also collaborates with Champions and Friends of UNICEF from diverse talents, disciplines, and backgrounds, including the arts, music, film, medicine, nutrition, sport, and content creation.
These individuals serve as powerful advocates, sharing their time and passion to help advance child rights so that all children can grow up healthy, educated, protected, and able to fulfil their potential.
These partnerships contribute to UNICEF’s broader work, implemented in partnership with the Government of Indonesia, civil society, the private sector, academia, media, and young people themselves.
For more information about UNICEF Indonesia works with National Ambassadors, Champions and high-profile personalities, visit: Influencers

**Jakarta, 10 February 2026** – UNICEF Indonesia today officially announced the appointment of Cinta Laura Kiehl as its new National Ambassador during a media event held at the National Library of Indonesia. The appointment highlights the important role public figures play in mobilizing support and advancing the rights and well-being of children across the country.
Cinta Laura brings to the role a long-standing commitment to social issues, particularly those affecting children and young people. Prior to her appointment, she has supported various UNICEF initiatives, including campaigns on child marriage prevention, and children’s right to education. Through her strong public reach and ability to inspire, she aims to help bring children’s issues into everyday conversations and amplify the voices of children and young people across Indonesia.
In late 2025, Cinta Laura visited Asmat, Papua, with UNICEF, where she witnessed firsthand the challenges facing children and families in remote and underserved communities and the ongoing efforts to address them. The visit provided an opportunity to see how UNICEF is working with the Government of Indonesia in strengthening essential services for children, including health, nutrition, education and child protection.
“Being appointed as UNICEF Indonesia’s National Ambassador is, for me, a deeply personal moral responsibility,” said Cinta Laura. “I have always believed that potential is evenly distributed, but sadly, opportunities are not.”
“When I visited Asmat, Papua, I witnessed firsthand how intelligent and resilient the children are, despite the extremely limited facilities around them. That experience deeply moved me and strengthened my commitment to ensuring their fundamental rights are fulfilled—the right to grow up safe, healthy, and surrounded by care. Together with UNICEF, we must accelerate our efforts to close this gap and build an ecosystem where every child has an equal starting point, so no child is left behind from the future they deserve.”
Speaking at the launch, Maniza Zaman, UNICEF Representative to Indonesia, welcomed Cinta Laura to UNICEF’s global family of ambassadors.
texts.1:
“Public figures play an important role in making children’s rights visible and relatable. They have the ability to inspire others and mobilize them as champions for children,” said Maniza Zaman. “Cinta brings authenticity, curiosity, and a genuine willingness to engage with the realities of children’s lives. UNICEF looks forward to a meaningful partnership with our new National Ambassador, so that together we can shine a light on the challenges, the progress, and the solutions needed for every child’s rights to be fully realized”.
As National Ambassador, Cinta Laura will support UNICEF Indonesia’s advocacy efforts by raising awareness on key child rights issues, including education, child protection, girls’ empowerment, and climate action. Her voice will play a vital role in encouraging collective action to create a more inclusive and equitable future for every child.
This appointment comes as UNICEF approaches its 80th anniversary globally in December 2026, underscoring the organization’s longstanding and continued commitment to protecting and promoting the rights of all children.
texts.2:
####
NOTE TO THE EDITOR:
UNICEF has a long history of working with influential figures to support child rights advocacy, dating back to 1954 when actor Danny Kaye was appointed as UNICEF’s first Goodwill Ambassador. Among UNICEF’s prominent global Goodwill Ambassadors are Audrey Hepburn, Sir Roger Moore, Jackie Chan, Sir David Beckham and Leo Messi.
In Indonesia, UNICEF appointed Ferry Salim as its first National Ambassador in 2004, a role he continues to hold. In addition to National Ambassadors, UNICEF Indonesia also collaborates with Champions and Friends of UNICEF from diverse talents, disciplines, and backgrounds, including the arts, music, film, medicine, nutrition, sport, and content creation.
These individuals serve as powerful advocates, sharing their time and passion to help advance child rights so that all children can grow up healthy, educated, protected, and able to fulfil their potential.
These partnerships contribute to UNICEF’s broader work, implemented in partnership with the Government of Indonesia, civil society, the private sector, academia, media, and young people themselves.
For more information about UNICEF Indonesia works with National Ambassadors, Champions and high-profile personalities, visit: Influencers

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Her adorable depiction of sneaking a glance at her crush through donuts in SPC Group's Happy Point Card commercial went viral in 2008.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-113) In February 2009, Etude House announced their exclusive model contract with Park, which was signed in January. She worked as a model for Etude, featuring alongside her _[You're Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Beautiful\_(TV\_series) "You're Beautiful (TV series)")_ co-star, Jang Keun-suk.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-114)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-115) Later, Etude paired her with Lee Min-ho.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-116) In the same year, she was paired with Kim Hyun-joong for a commercial for Coca-Cola's carbonated beverage Dynamic Kin.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-117) Additionally, she worked with CJ Foodville's VIPS and Korea Fujifilm's Instax Mini camera.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:14-110) In 2012, Park was chosen as the exclusive model for Gounsesang Cosmetics.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-118)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2013, following the success of _Miracle in Cell No. 7_ and tvN's _My Cute Guys,_ Park became more popular. She appeared in Orion's Market O Valentine's Day commercial alongside Yoon Si-yoon, Kim Ji-hoon, and Ko Kyung-pyo from _My Cute Guys_. Park collaborated with various brands such as Sonobi,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-119) Jambaengi,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-120) Enprani Holika Holika,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-121) job search portal Job Sarangbang,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-122) The K Non-life Insurance Educar,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-123) and health drink Vegemil.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-124)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
The success of the drama _The Heirs_ further boosted Park's endorsement opportunities. In 2014, Park appeared in a commercial for local delivery app Yogiyo with her costar Kang Ha-neul.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-125) Park reunited with Jang Keun-suk in a Chinese beverage brand ad to celebrate the brand's 15th anniversary in 2014.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-126) She was the first Korean star to be selected as a model for [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc.").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-127) Since the 2014 F/W season, Park served as the muse for the French jewellery brand Agatha Paris.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-128)
After her hit drama _Pinocchio,_ Park endorsed several international brands[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-endorsement-129) including the Italian brand Bruno Magli and the French outdoor clothing brand Millet.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-131) After the success of the drama _The Doctors_, it has been reported that brands like Bruno Magli experienced a surge in sales as a result of Park's endorsements.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-132)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2017, Park made history as the first Korean to serve as a global ambassador of Swarovski.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-133)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-134) She was also selected as the Korean muse for Coach[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-135) and Filipino clothing brand Bench.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-136) In 2018, Park was chosen as the exclusive model of bedding brand Allerman.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-137)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-138) In 2019, Park was chosen as first-ever brand ambassador for Korea by British jewellery brand Olivia Burton.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-139) Since 2019, she has been the muse for the clothing brand MOJO.S.PHINE.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-140) In 2021, she was chosen as the new model for the French original golf wear brand Castelbajac.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-141)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park Shin-hye has been engaged in volunteering organized by the church with her family since she was a child, taking part in initiatives such as the "Babfor Sharing Movement"[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-Babfor-144) and Habitat for Humanity.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:6-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-146) She expanded her philanthropic efforts after entering the entertainment industry through Starlight Angel Project.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:10-147)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-148)
In 2007, Park donated her talent for the omnibus drama Several Questions That Make Us Happy[ko]. The drama's proceeds, excluding production costs, were donated, including the fees of the writers, directors, and actors. The drama aimed to emphasize the significance of volunteering in a challenging social environment. It involved notable writers such as Noh Hee-kyung, Lee Sun-hee, and Seo Hee-jung, and was directed by Sung Joon-gi, with KBS producers Kim Yong-soo and Hong Seok-gu overseeing the project.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:12-30)
In late 2009, Park travelled to Tapatali village in Nepal, for a six-day visit. During her stay, Park distributed school supplies to children in need, helped break and carry stones for those working in the quarry, and dressed up as Santa Claus to give special Christmas gifts to the villagers. This volunteer experience was featured in the KBS Love Request year-end special broadcast 'Home Winter Love'.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-149)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-150)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2010, Park participated in CeCi magazine's "I Love Pet" campaign to celebrate the magazine's 16th anniversary. The campaign promoted adopting abandoned dogs through organizations like 'Animal Freedom Solidarity' and supported service animals through the 'Animal-assisted Therapy Welfare Association', which provides emotional therapy for disabled children with trained animals.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-151)
In 2011, Park became a public relations ambassador for "Korea Food for the Hungry International" (hereinafter referred to as KFHI).[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) As part of her role, she volunteered in Ghana for 8 nights and 9 days in May. During her time there, Park delivered food kits to impoverished children, assisted children with malaria treatment, and spent quality time with a sponsored child named Avanna, taking care of her and sharing meals together. This KFHI's campaign was showcased in the television documentary "2011 MBC World Food Day Special - Stop the Hunger Sharing Campaign."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-153)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-154)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park also participated in initiatives in response to the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. To celebrate the airing of the drama _Heartstrings_ on Fuji TV Japan, Park and Jung Yong-hwa held a meet and greet event on July 15 and 16, 2012 at the Tokyo International Forum Hall. The event was attended by approximately 10,000 fans, and a portion of the proceeds was donated through KFHI[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) for Tōhoku survivors.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-155)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-156) In August 2012, the non-profit organization "Good Friends Save Children" (GFSC) organized a fundraising event called "Hopes, Dreams, Happy Trip to Korea." The event invited 80 students and staff from Ogatsu Middle School in Ishinomaki, Miyagi Prefecture, representing the Tōhoku survivors. Park, Jung Yong-hwa and Lee Hong-gi appeared as surprise guests, providing words of encouragement and gifts.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-157)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-158)

South Korean actress Park Shin Hye has once again touched hearts with her generosity.
On March 13, her agency SALT Entertainment shared that the actress donated 100 million won (around $67,000) to help single-parent families in need. The donation will be used to provide essential support such as living expenses and child-rearing assistance.
The contribution is part of the “Starlight Angel Project,” a meaningful initiative she has carried out with her fans since 2012. Through the program, Park Shin Hye and her fandom continue to support people facing difficult circumstances.
The funds were given through Korea Food for the Hungry International (KFHI), an international relief organization where the actress serves as an ambassador.
Park Shin Hye shared that filming her drama Undercover Miss Hong made her reflect deeply on the struggles faced by single-parent families. She expressed her hope that the donation can bring warmth, comfort, and real help to those going through similar hardships.
KFHI also expressed gratitude, noting that single-parent households often carry both financial and caregiving responsibilities alone, and that this donation will help children grow up in a more stable environment.

Published October 19, 2017 - 8:43 p.m.
Make us preferred on Google
Actor Park Shin-hye has been appointed the global ambassador of renowned jewelry brand Swarovski, according to her agency S.A.L.T. Entertainment. She has been the brand ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016. Swarovski is an Austrian brand that specializes in precision cut crystal which was established in 1895.
With the news, Swarovski released new photos of Park holding gifts in a red dress and wearing crystal accessories from the brand. The image will hang in stores in more than 120 countries around the world.

# Park Shin-hye named Swarovski ambassador
Former global ambassadors for the brand include former Victoria’s Secret Angel and supermodel Miranda Kerr and American model Karlie Kloss. This is first time a Korean has been selected the brand’s global ambassador, and it is unconventional for an actress to be chosen instead of a professional model, according to Ilgan Sports, an affiliate of Korea JoongAng Daily.
An insider at Swarovski explained to Ilgan Sports that “[Park] has been the ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016, and through movies, dramas and charities she has not only spread her influence worldwide but has also showed her dynamism, which the brand pursues.”
Meanwhile, Park has been cast as a lawyer in the movie “Heart Blackened” which will be released in Nov. 2.

[March 13](https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=pfbid029mUXW6vy3x2cLGw1gddaJHfDXsrUBkLw5Pa45ByTJQnJyAAJE6scVWDANsp7K67Fl&id=100038851646507&__cft__[0]=AZiQENofpekGtfbI9KAQL-Q1OdkyAKkXcWLYovg8uQwKbfv9oXA6e6iYVmEhzA99Crtygo3rQzeW6FszyFLiK1iDjHWfQ28X4VdYX5ifjK4QhxNwrYP_l-vJsHuQwLHgDjJmdeWJ3CXYftzAkiE3iecqDSU3xQwP&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) ·
South Korean actress Park Shin Hye has once again touched hearts with her generosity.
On March 13, her agency SALT Entertainment shared that the actress donated 100 million won (around $67,000) to help single-parent families in need. The donation will be used to provide essential support such as living expenses and child-rearing assistance.
The contribution is part of the “Starlight Angel Project,” a meaningful initiative she has carried out with her fans since 2012. Through the program, Park Shin Hye and her fandom continue to support people facing difficult circumstances.
The funds were given through Korea Food for the Hungry International (KFHI), an international relief organization where the actress serves as an ambassador.
Park Shin Hye shared that filming her drama Undercover Miss Hong made her reflect deeply on the struggles faced by single-parent families. She expressed her hope that the donation can bring warmth, comfort, and real help to those going through similar hardships.
KFHI also expressed gratitude, noting that single-parent households often carry both financial and caregiving responsibilities alone, and that this donation will help children grow up in a more stable environment.

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Her adorable depiction of sneaking a glance at her crush through donuts in SPC Group's Happy Point Card commercial went viral in 2008.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-113) In February 2009, Etude House announced their exclusive model contract with Park, which was signed in January. She worked as a model for Etude, featuring alongside her _[You're Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Beautiful\_(TV\_series) "You're Beautiful (TV series)")_ co-star, Jang Keun-suk.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-114)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-115) Later, Etude paired her with Lee Min-ho.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-116) In the same year, she was paired with Kim Hyun-joong for a commercial for Coca-Cola's carbonated beverage Dynamic Kin.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-117) Additionally, she worked with CJ Foodville's VIPS and Korea Fujifilm's Instax Mini camera.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:14-110) In 2012, Park was chosen as the exclusive model for Gounsesang Cosmetics.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-118)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park Shin-hye has been engaged in volunteering organized by the church with her family since she was a child, taking part in initiatives such as the "Babfor Sharing Movement"[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-Babfor-144) and Habitat for Humanity.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:6-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-146) She expanded her philanthropic efforts after entering the entertainment industry through Starlight Angel Project.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:10-147)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-148)
In 2007, Park donated her talent for the omnibus drama Several Questions That Make Us Happy[ko]. The drama's proceeds, excluding production costs, were donated, including the fees of the writers, directors, and actors. The drama aimed to emphasize the significance of volunteering in a challenging social environment. It involved notable writers such as Noh Hee-kyung, Lee Sun-hee, and Seo Hee-jung, and was directed by Sung Joon-gi, with KBS producers Kim Yong-soo and Hong Seok-gu overseeing the project.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:12-30)
In late 2009, Park travelled to Tapatali village in Nepal, for a six-day visit. During her stay, Park distributed school supplies to children in need, helped break and carry stones for those working in the quarry, and dressed up as Santa Claus to give special Christmas gifts to the villagers. This volunteer experience was featured in the KBS Love Request year-end special broadcast 'Home Winter Love'.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-149)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-150)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2010, Park participated in CeCi magazine's "I Love Pet" campaign to celebrate the magazine's 16th anniversary. The campaign promoted adopting abandoned dogs through organizations like 'Animal Freedom Solidarity' and supported service animals through the 'Animal-assisted Therapy Welfare Association', which provides emotional therapy for disabled children with trained animals.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-151)
In 2011, Park became a public relations ambassador for "Korea Food for the Hungry International" (hereinafter referred to as KFHI).[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) As part of her role, she volunteered in Ghana for 8 nights and 9 days in May. During her time there, Park delivered food kits to impoverished children, assisted children with malaria treatment, and spent quality time with a sponsored child named Avanna, taking care of her and sharing meals together. This KFHI's campaign was showcased in the television documentary "2011 MBC World Food Day Special - Stop the Hunger Sharing Campaign."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-153)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-154)
texts.24:
## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park also participated in initiatives in response to the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. To celebrate the airing of the drama _Heartstrings_ on Fuji TV Japan, Park and Jung Yong-hwa held a meet and greet event on July 15 and 16, 2012 at the Tokyo International Forum Hall. The event was attended by approximately 10,000 fans, and a portion of the proceeds was donated through KFHI[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) for Tōhoku survivors.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-155)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-156) In August 2012, the non-profit organization "Good Friends Save Children" (GFSC) organized a fundraising event called "Hopes, Dreams, Happy Trip to Korea." The event invited 80 students and staff from Ogatsu Middle School in Ishinomaki, Miyagi Prefecture, representing the Tōhoku survivors. Park, Jung Yong-hwa and Lee Hong-gi appeared as surprise guests, providing words of encouragement and gifts.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-157)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-158)

Published October 19, 2017 - 8:43 p.m.
Make us preferred on Google
Actor Park Shin-hye has been appointed the global ambassador of renowned jewelry brand Swarovski, according to her agency S.A.L.T. Entertainment. She has been the brand ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016. Swarovski is an Austrian brand that specializes in precision cut crystal which was established in 1895.
With the news, Swarovski released new photos of Park holding gifts in a red dress and wearing crystal accessories from the brand. The image will hang in stores in more than 120 countries around the world.

# Park Shin-hye named Swarovski ambassador
Former global ambassadors for the brand include former Victoria’s Secret Angel and supermodel Miranda Kerr and American model Karlie Kloss. This is first time a Korean has been selected the brand’s global ambassador, and it is unconventional for an actress to be chosen instead of a professional model, according to Ilgan Sports, an affiliate of Korea JoongAng Daily.
An insider at Swarovski explained to Ilgan Sports that “[Park] has been the ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016, and through movies, dramas and charities she has not only spread her influence worldwide but has also showed her dynamism, which the brand pursues.”
Meanwhile, Park has been cast as a lawyer in the movie “Heart Blackened” which will be released in Nov. 2.
By Hong You-kyoung

# Yuna Kim
UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador since 2010
< Back to Goodwill Ambassadors
UNICEF/UNI94576/Markisz
> “I want to use my own positive experience to help the millions of vulnerable children around the world. Even in the hardest circumstances, dreams can give you the courage to live, and I hope I can share that message with children in need."  
>   
> Yuna Kim, Republic of Korea
International skating sensation Yuna Kim was appointed UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador on 12 July 2010, just months after winning Olympic gold in women’s single skating in Vancouver, Canada.
Yuna has long been supportive of UNICEF’s work on behalf of the world’s children, and became especially motivated to step up her engagement following the devastating earthquake in Haiti on 12 January 2010.
Since then, she has continuously supported UNICEF campaigns for the world’s most vulnerable children, including children displaced by Syria, children affected by Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines, and children affected by the earthquake in Nepal, as well as campaigns to promote children’s rights around the world, like #NoLostGeneration, #LikeYUNA and #SportsForEveryChild.

> “I want to use my own positive experience to help the millions of vulnerable children around the world. Even in the hardest circumstances, dreams can give you the courage to live, and I hope I can share that message with children in need."  
>   
> Yuna Kim, Republic of Korea
International skating sensation Yuna Kim was appointed UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador on 12 July 2010, just months after winning Olympic gold in women’s single skating in Vancouver, Canada.
Yuna has long been supportive of UNICEF’s work on behalf of the world’s children, and became especially motivated to step up her engagement following the devastating earthquake in Haiti on 12 January 2010.
Since then, she has continuously supported UNICEF campaigns for the world’s most vulnerable children, including children displaced by Syria, children affected by Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines, and children affected by the earthquake in Nepal, as well as campaigns to promote children’s rights around the world, like #NoLostGeneration, #LikeYUNA and #SportsForEveryChild.

# Yuna Kim
UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador since 2010
< Back to Goodwill Ambassadors
UNICEF/UNI94576/Markisz
> “I want to use my own positive experience to help the millions of vulnerable children around the world. Even in the hardest circumstances, dreams can give you the courage to live, and I hope I can share that message with children in need."  
>   
> Yuna Kim, Republic of Korea
International skating sensation Yuna Kim was appointed UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador on 12 July 2010, just months after winning Olympic gold in women’s single skating in Vancouver, Canada.
Yuna has long been supportive of UNICEF’s work on behalf of the world’s children, and became especially motivated to step up her engagement following the devastating earthquake in Haiti on 12 January 2010.
Since then, she has continuously supported UNICEF campaigns for the world’s most vulnerable children, including children displaced by Syria, children affected by Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines, and children affected by the earthquake in Nepal, as well as campaigns to promote children’s rights around the world, like #NoLostGeneration, #LikeYUNA and #SportsForEveryChild.

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Her adorable depiction of sneaking a glance at her crush through donuts in SPC Group's Happy Point Card commercial went viral in 2008.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-113) In February 2009, Etude House announced their exclusive model contract with Park, which was signed in January. She worked as a model for Etude, featuring alongside her _[You're Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Beautiful\_(TV\_series) "You're Beautiful (TV series)")_ co-star, Jang Keun-suk.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-114)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-115) Later, Etude paired her with Lee Min-ho.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-116) In the same year, she was paired with Kim Hyun-joong for a commercial for Coca-Cola's carbonated beverage Dynamic Kin.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-117) Additionally, she worked with CJ Foodville's VIPS and Korea Fujifilm's Instax Mini camera.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:14-110) In 2012, Park was chosen as the exclusive model for Gounsesang Cosmetics.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-118)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2013, following the success of _Miracle in Cell No. 7_ and tvN's _My Cute Guys,_ Park became more popular. She appeared in Orion's Market O Valentine's Day commercial alongside Yoon Si-yoon, Kim Ji-hoon, and Ko Kyung-pyo from _My Cute Guys_. Park collaborated with various brands such as Sonobi,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-119) Jambaengi,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-120) Enprani Holika Holika,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-121) job search portal Job Sarangbang,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-122) The K Non-life Insurance Educar,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-123) and health drink Vegemil.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-124)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
The success of the drama _The Heirs_ further boosted Park's endorsement opportunities. In 2014, Park appeared in a commercial for local delivery app Yogiyo with her costar Kang Ha-neul.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-125) Park reunited with Jang Keun-suk in a Chinese beverage brand ad to celebrate the brand's 15th anniversary in 2014.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-126) She was the first Korean star to be selected as a model for [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc.").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-127) Since the 2014 F/W season, Park served as the muse for the French jewellery brand Agatha Paris.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-128)
After her hit drama _Pinocchio,_ Park endorsed several international brands[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-endorsement-129) including the Italian brand Bruno Magli and the French outdoor clothing brand Millet.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-131) After the success of the drama _The Doctors_, it has been reported that brands like Bruno Magli experienced a surge in sales as a result of Park's endorsements.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-132)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2017, Park made history as the first Korean to serve as a global ambassador of Swarovski.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-133)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-134) She was also selected as the Korean muse for Coach[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-135) and Filipino clothing brand Bench.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-136) In 2018, Park was chosen as the exclusive model of bedding brand Allerman.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-137)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-138) In 2019, Park was chosen as first-ever brand ambassador for Korea by British jewellery brand Olivia Burton.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-139) Since 2019, she has been the muse for the clothing brand MOJO.S.PHINE.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-140) In 2021, she was chosen as the new model for the French original golf wear brand Castelbajac.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-141)
This section **may need to be rewritten to comply with Wikipedia's quality standards**, as it currently reads as a WP:PROSELINE list of events. Relevant discussion may be found on the talk page. You can help. The talk page may contain suggestions._(January 2026)_

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park Shin-hye has been engaged in volunteering organized by the church with her family since she was a child, taking part in initiatives such as the "Babfor Sharing Movement"[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-Babfor-144) and Habitat for Humanity.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:6-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-146) She expanded her philanthropic efforts after entering the entertainment industry through Starlight Angel Project.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:10-147)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-148)
In 2007, Park donated her talent for the omnibus drama Several Questions That Make Us Happy[ko]. The drama's proceeds, excluding production costs, were donated, including the fees of the writers, directors, and actors. The drama aimed to emphasize the significance of volunteering in a challenging social environment. It involved notable writers such as Noh Hee-kyung, Lee Sun-hee, and Seo Hee-jung, and was directed by Sung Joon-gi, with KBS producers Kim Yong-soo and Hong Seok-gu overseeing the project.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:12-30)
In late 2009, Park travelled to Tapatali village in Nepal, for a six-day visit. During her stay, Park distributed school supplies to children in need, helped break and carry stones for those working in the quarry, and dressed up as Santa Claus to give special Christmas gifts to the villagers. This volunteer experience was featured in the KBS Love Request year-end special broadcast 'Home Winter Love'.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-149)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-150)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2010, Park participated in CeCi magazine's "I Love Pet" campaign to celebrate the magazine's 16th anniversary. The campaign promoted adopting abandoned dogs through organizations like 'Animal Freedom Solidarity' and supported service animals through the 'Animal-assisted Therapy Welfare Association', which provides emotional therapy for disabled children with trained animals.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-151)
In 2011, Park became a public relations ambassador for "Korea Food for the Hungry International" (hereinafter referred to as KFHI).[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) As part of her role, she volunteered in Ghana for 8 nights and 9 days in May. During her time there, Park delivered food kits to impoverished children, assisted children with malaria treatment, and spent quality time with a sponsored child named Avanna, taking care of her and sharing meals together. This KFHI's campaign was showcased in the television documentary "2011 MBC World Food Day Special - Stop the Hunger Sharing Campaign."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-153)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-154)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park also participated in initiatives in response to the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. To celebrate the airing of the drama _Heartstrings_ on Fuji TV Japan, Park and Jung Yong-hwa held a meet and greet event on July 15 and 16, 2012 at the Tokyo International Forum Hall. The event was attended by approximately 10,000 fans, and a portion of the proceeds was donated through KFHI[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) for Tōhoku survivors.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-155)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-156) In August 2012, the non-profit organization "Good Friends Save Children" (GFSC) organized a fundraising event called "Hopes, Dreams, Happy Trip to Korea." The event invited 80 students and staff from Ogatsu Middle School in Ishinomaki, Miyagi Prefecture, representing the Tōhoku survivors. Park, Jung Yong-hwa and Lee Hong-gi appeared as surprise guests, providing words of encouragement and gifts.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-157)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-158)

Published October 19, 2017 - 8:43 p.m.
Make us preferred on Google
Actor Park Shin-hye has been appointed the global ambassador of renowned jewelry brand Swarovski, according to her agency S.A.L.T. Entertainment. She has been the brand ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016. Swarovski is an Austrian brand that specializes in precision cut crystal which was established in 1895.
With the news, Swarovski released new photos of Park holding gifts in a red dress and wearing crystal accessories from the brand. The image will hang in stores in more than 120 countries around the world.

# Park Shin-hye named Swarovski ambassador
Former global ambassadors for the brand include former Victoria’s Secret Angel and supermodel Miranda Kerr and American model Karlie Kloss. This is first time a Korean has been selected the brand’s global ambassador, and it is unconventional for an actress to be chosen instead of a professional model, according to Ilgan Sports, an affiliate of Korea JoongAng Daily.
An insider at Swarovski explained to Ilgan Sports that “[Park] has been the ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016, and through movies, dramas and charities she has not only spread her influence worldwide but has also showed her dynamism, which the brand pursues.”
Meanwhile, Park has been cast as a lawyer in the movie “Heart Blackened” which will be released in Nov. 2.
By Hong You-kyoung

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Her adorable depiction of sneaking a glance at her crush through donuts in SPC Group's Happy Point Card commercial went viral in 2008.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-113) In February 2009, Etude House announced their exclusive model contract with Park, which was signed in January. She worked as a model for Etude, featuring alongside her _[You're Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Beautiful\_(TV\_series) "You're Beautiful (TV series)")_ co-star, Jang Keun-suk.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-114)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-115) Later, Etude paired her with Lee Min-ho.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-116) In the same year, she was paired with Kim Hyun-joong for a commercial for Coca-Cola's carbonated beverage Dynamic Kin.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-117) Additionally, she worked with CJ Foodville's VIPS and Korea Fujifilm's Instax Mini camera.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:14-110) In 2012, Park was chosen as the exclusive model for Gounsesang Cosmetics.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-118)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2013, following the success of _Miracle in Cell No. 7_ and tvN's _My Cute Guys,_ Park became more popular. She appeared in Orion's Market O Valentine's Day commercial alongside Yoon Si-yoon, Kim Ji-hoon, and Ko Kyung-pyo from _My Cute Guys_. Park collaborated with various brands such as Sonobi,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-119) Jambaengi,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-120) Enprani Holika Holika,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-121) job search portal Job Sarangbang,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-122) The K Non-life Insurance Educar,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-123) and health drink Vegemil.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-124)
texts.20:
## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
The success of the drama _The Heirs_ further boosted Park's endorsement opportunities. In 2014, Park appeared in a commercial for local delivery app Yogiyo with her costar Kang Ha-neul.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-125) Park reunited with Jang Keun-suk in a Chinese beverage brand ad to celebrate the brand's 15th anniversary in 2014.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-126) She was the first Korean star to be selected as a model for [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc.").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-127) Since the 2014 F/W season, Park served as the muse for the French jewellery brand Agatha Paris.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-128)
After her hit drama _Pinocchio,_ Park endorsed several international brands[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-endorsement-129) including the Italian brand Bruno Magli and the French outdoor clothing brand Millet.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-131) After the success of the drama _The Doctors_, it has been reported that brands like Bruno Magli experienced a surge in sales as a result of Park's endorsements.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-132)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2017, Park made history as the first Korean to serve as a global ambassador of Swarovski.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-133)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-134) She was also selected as the Korean muse for Coach[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-135) and Filipino clothing brand Bench.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-136) In 2018, Park was chosen as the exclusive model of bedding brand Allerman.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-137)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-138) In 2019, Park was chosen as first-ever brand ambassador for Korea by British jewellery brand Olivia Burton.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-139) Since 2019, she has been the muse for the clothing brand MOJO.S.PHINE.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-140) In 2021, she was chosen as the new model for the French original golf wear brand Castelbajac.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-141)

## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park Shin-hye has been engaged in volunteering organized by the church with her family since she was a child, taking part in initiatives such as the "Babfor Sharing Movement"[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-Babfor-144) and Habitat for Humanity.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:6-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-146) She expanded her philanthropic efforts after entering the entertainment industry through Starlight Angel Project.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:10-147)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-148)
In 2007, Park donated her talent for the omnibus drama Several Questions That Make Us Happy[ko]. The drama's proceeds, excluding production costs, were donated, including the fees of the writers, directors, and actors. The drama aimed to emphasize the significance of volunteering in a challenging social environment. It involved notable writers such as Noh Hee-kyung, Lee Sun-hee, and Seo Hee-jung, and was directed by Sung Joon-gi, with KBS producers Kim Yong-soo and Hong Seok-gu overseeing the project.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-:12-30)
In late 2009, Park travelled to Tapatali village in Nepal, for a six-day visit. During her stay, Park distributed school supplies to children in need, helped break and carry stones for those working in the quarry, and dressed up as Santa Claus to give special Christmas gifts to the villagers. This volunteer experience was featured in the KBS Love Request year-end special broadcast 'Home Winter Love'.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-149)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-150)
texts.23:
## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
In 2010, Park participated in CeCi magazine's "I Love Pet" campaign to celebrate the magazine's 16th anniversary. The campaign promoted adopting abandoned dogs through organizations like 'Animal Freedom Solidarity' and supported service animals through the 'Animal-assisted Therapy Welfare Association', which provides emotional therapy for disabled children with trained animals.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-151)
In 2011, Park became a public relations ambassador for "Korea Food for the Hungry International" (hereinafter referred to as KFHI).[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) As part of her role, she volunteered in Ghana for 8 nights and 9 days in May. During her time there, Park delivered food kits to impoverished children, assisted children with malaria treatment, and spent quality time with a sponsored child named Avanna, taking care of her and sharing meals together. This KFHI's campaign was showcased in the television documentary "2011 MBC World Food Day Special - Stop the Hunger Sharing Campaign."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-153)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-154)
texts.24:
## Early life and education
### 2023–present: Established actress
Park also participated in initiatives in response to the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. To celebrate the airing of the drama _Heartstrings_ on Fuji TV Japan, Park and Jung Yong-hwa held a meet and greet event on July 15 and 16, 2012 at the Tokyo International Forum Hall. The event was attended by approximately 10,000 fans, and a portion of the proceeds was donated through KFHI[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-KFHI-152) for Tōhoku survivors.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-155)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-156) In August 2012, the non-profit organization "Good Friends Save Children" (GFSC) organized a fundraising event called "Hopes, Dreams, Happy Trip to Korea." The event invited 80 students and staff from Ogatsu Middle School in Ishinomaki, Miyagi Prefecture, representing the Tōhoku survivors. Park, Jung Yong-hwa and Lee Hong-gi appeared as surprise guests, providing words of encouragement and gifts.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-157)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Shin-hye#cite_note-158)

Published October 19, 2017 - 8:43 p.m.
Make us preferred on Google
Actor Park Shin-hye has been appointed the global ambassador of renowned jewelry brand Swarovski, according to her agency S.A.L.T. Entertainment. She has been the brand ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016. Swarovski is an Austrian brand that specializes in precision cut crystal which was established in 1895.
With the news, Swarovski released new photos of Park holding gifts in a red dress and wearing crystal accessories from the brand. The image will hang in stores in more than 120 countries around the world.
texts.2:
# Park Shin-hye named Swarovski ambassador
Former global ambassadors for the brand include former Victoria’s Secret Angel and supermodel Miranda Kerr and American model Karlie Kloss. This is first time a Korean has been selected the brand’s global ambassador, and it is unconventional for an actress to be chosen instead of a professional model, according to Ilgan Sports, an affiliate of Korea JoongAng Daily.
An insider at Swarovski explained to Ilgan Sports that “[Park] has been the ambassador of Swarovski Korea since 2016, and through movies, dramas and charities she has not only spread her influence worldwide but has also showed her dynamism, which the brand pursues.”
Meanwhile, Park has been cast as a lawyer in the movie “Heart Blackened” which will be released in Nov. 2.
By Hong You-kyoung
